newsitem.title: USA: Kinnard settles with Minn. Commerce Dept..
newsitem.headline: Kinnard settles with Minn. Commerce Dept..

text.p: The Minnesota Department of Commerce said Friday it has reached a settlement with John G. Kinnard and Co Inc on allegations that the company violated securities regulations in connection with the offer and sale of investments issued by Citi-Equity Group.

From September 1989 through July 1993, Kinnard raised more than $29 million from the sale of Citi-Equity Group limited partnerships and mortgage offerings, according to statements issued by the company and the Minnesota Commerce Department.

Under the agreement, Kinnard said it will pay a fine of $225,000 to the State of Minnesota in addition to a payment of $100,000 to reimburse for the costs of its investigation. Kinnard also said it agreed to undertake a review of its sales practices and procedures.

Kinnard said the company neither admits or denies any wrongdoing. "Because Kinnard believed the legal defense costs alone could have exceeded the amount paid, it chose to settle and avoid distracting its employees from their main focus of serving investors," the company said in a statement.
Kinnard said its 1996 financial results included a reserve towards these settlement costs.
Most of the civil liability issues relating to the Citi-Equity transactions were already resolved by a court-approved class action settlement in December 1995, the Commerce Department said.
John G. Kinnard is a subsidiary of Kinnard Investments Inc.
